Print, Summary, Tidy and Recipe-Step Methods for TempleCBE Classes

Source: R/as_tuning_results.R, R/audit_render_parity.R, R/balance_diagnostics.R, and 20 more
templecbe_methods.Rd

S3 methods of the classes that TempleCBE functions return, for generics of base R, generics, dplyr and recipes. They are called through the generic (`print(x)`, `summary(x)`, `tidy(x)`, `x$name`, ...), not by their full name. The help page of the function that creates each class describes the object; this page records the methods that have no page of their own.

Arguments

...

Passed to other methods, or not used.

x, object

An object of the class named after the dot in the method.

max_print

Largest number of differences to print for each table.

y

A second object of the same class as `x`.

node_by, edge_by

Columns that identify a node and an edge when two databases are combined. `node_by = NULL` uses the node name.

name

Name of the element to extract.

training

The training data from which a step is estimated.

info

The variable table of the recipe (name, type, role, source).

new_data

A data frame to which a trained step is applied.

width

Width of the printed line.

Value

`print()` methods return `x` invisibly. `summary()` and `tidy()` methods return a tibble or a list of tibbles. `$` returns the element. The set operations return a database. `prep()` returns the trained step, `bake()` the transformed data, `tunable()` a tibble of tunable arguments and `required_pkgs()` a character vector of package names.

Details

* `print()` methods write a short description of the object to the console and return it invisibly. * `summary()` and `tidy()` methods return a tibble (or a list of tibbles) with the content of the object. * `$` methods give access to elements under their current names, and under former names with a deprecation warning. * `union()`, `intersect()` and `setdiff()` for a database (see [as_database()]) combine the nodes and the edges of two databases. * `prep()`, `bake()`, `tidy()`, `tunable()` and `required_pkgs()` are the methods that recipes calls for the steps [step_famd()], [step_lencode_coxnet()] and [step_lencode_joint_model()].
